R1/R2/R3/R3.5 impact-scope regression must pass on this stage's
candidate, with no unexplained skip.
Section 5.2 is explicit that citing an old ACCEPTED verdict does not
show a refactor did not regress. So this names the suites that the
interface work could reach and requires them to be RUN here, not
referenced.
The list is frozen at the start of the stage. A suite added later to
make a number look better is the thing a frozen list prevents.
why_these: The interface work of this stage touched: the device testbench and
the public top (rtl/tnca_shell.v), the core's reset list, the
transport and backend interfaces, the runtime's argument upload, the
compile target's platform_binding split, and the TTIR importer.
Everything downstream of those is in scope.

note: Section 5.2 freezes the NEW run list and its caps: '阶段启动时冻结新增运行
清单、次数、cycle/wall 上限'. The caps below come from
spec/r36_required_cases.json and bound what THIS stage adds -- the
Re-running the inherited regression is required by R36-TEST-02 and is
not a new run. Its cost is measured and recorded, and it is NOT
charged against the new-run cap: doing so would fail the gate for the
size of a suite this stage did not create, which is a verdict about
the wrong thing. The first version of this file made that mistake.

new_runs.charged_to: every tools/r36 checker except `regression`, which re-runs inherited suites
new_runs.over_budget: stays a failure. The contract forbids re-running until it fits.

inherited.why: these suites existed before this stage and their runtime is a property of them, not of this work. The figure is recorded so a change in it is visible.

budget.accounting: subprocess by subprocess. A checker that reuses one run for several cases counts it once, which is why the conformance suite opens one device per backend rather than one per case.

about: Targets that must be built before the suites below can run, and the
reason each is needed. The scope was frozen without them, so on the
acceptance host -- a fresh clone with nothing built -- three suites
failed for missing artefacts rather than for anything about the
code: r1-ir-tests had no tnca-opt, r1-profile-tests had no
tb_core4.vvp, and r35-safety-tests' own clean baseline could not
measure L06.
The CI workflow has always built these before running the same
suites; the regression runner was the only caller that did not, and
it was also the only one claiming to reproduce them from a clean
checkout.

targets.why: the runtime reads python/tnca/data in preference to the working tree, and a fresh clone has none
the simulated device the runtime launches on
r1-ir-tests drives the MLIR tool; without it IR-01, IR-02, IR-05 and IR-07 report a missing binary
r1-profile-tests CFG-01 reads capabilities back from tb_core4.vvp, the four-context instance
the banked register file instance, which the delivery profile elaborates
the reference instance CFG-01 also reads back
the whole-machine instance CFG-01 reads back
